chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, that he said:
I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, about: «the male attendants with no carnality». He said: It is the dumb, the imposed, who does not (sexually) approach women.

key_terms.الْمَوْلَى عَلَيْهِ: the slave under the master's authority

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of 'non-carnal male attendants' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific category of 'non-carnal' male attendants (*ghulaman lahu ubun*) referenced in Quran 24:31, defining them as mute slaves who do not engage in sexual relations with women. This legal definition highlights the criteria for modesty and privacy within the household, ensuring that those serving as attendants do not possess the physical or communicative capacity to compromise the modesty of the women. The explanation underscores the practical application of Quranic verses regarding *khulwa* (seclusion) and the protection of women's honor in domestic settings.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from Hasan bin Ali al-Washhaa’, from Ali bin Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, that he said:
I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, about: « the male attendants with no carnality» [24:31]. He said: It is the dumb, the imposed, who does not (sexually) approach women.
